value.rationale: The natural rectangle order-ideal Wiener-distance problem has known first moments, but its complete fixed-two-row joint metric/inclusion distribution is a distinct structural question. Exact beta-binomial incomparability law and distinct comparable/incomparable limit populations quantify information lost by aggregate distance metrics, including a positive long-chord comparable tail. Motivated by minuscule lattices and canonical Euclidean order polytopes, not an arbitrary slice.
